analyses.localAcceptanceDetails: NOT accepted in standard curbside municipal recycling in almost all jurisdictions. Polystyrene cups are brittle, shatter into small fragments that ruin paper and glass recycling bales, and have virtually no viable commercial secondary markets.
preparationSteps: Do NOT place in your curbside blue recycling bin (it is considered a severe bale contaminant)
Rinse out beverage residue if reusing or repurposing at home
Look for specialized mail-in programs (such as TerraCycle Party Cup Zero Waste Box) if collecting in bulk
Otherwise discard in your general residual landfill waste bin
limitations: Shatters into brittle shards under compactor pressure in municipal collection trucks, contaminating paper hydrapulping tanks.
Extremely low bulk density and low market scrap value makes sorting and transport economically unviable for MRFs.
Optical ballistic separators misidentify thin flattened cups as paper sheets, leading to cross-contamination.
analyses.safeDisposalInstructions: Dispose of in the general residual/landfill bin. Avoid single-use plastic party cups in the future; consider reusable tumblers, washable glassware, or certified aluminum cups.

analyses.primaryObject: Metal ballpoint or rollerball pen with cap
analyses.material: Multi-material composite (Lacquered brass/steel exterior, ABS/POM internal threading, spring steel, tungsten carbide ball, residual dye/solvent ink)
analyses.localAcceptanceDetails: Austin Resource Recovery (City of Austin single-stream blue bin) does not accept writing utensils, pens, or small composite items. These multi-material items fall through disc screens and trommels at the Materials Recovery Facility (MRF) and contaminate metal or plastic recovery streams.
preparationSteps: Refill the pen with replacement ink cartridges instead of discarding the exterior body.
If disposing completely, unscrew and disassemble the pen into separate components (clip, barrel, spring, plastic feed, ink tube).
Remove and discard the ink cartridge in the municipal trash as the residual chemical ink contaminates recycling streams.
Collect pens and empty writing instruments for specialized mail-in recycling programs rather than curbside collection.
limitations: Size limitation: Objects smaller than 2-3 inches in two dimensions fall through MRF sorting screens directly into residue/landfill.
Multi-material bonding: Bonded metal, plastic internal sleeves, and lacquer finishes cannot be mechanically separated cost-effectively in municipal facilities.
Hazardous/chemical ink residues: Residual solvents and pigments contaminate plastic wash lines and metal smelting fluxes.
Lack of automated sorting: Optical sorters (NIR) fail on black lacquer and mixed metallic-plastic composite assemblies.
analyses.safeDisposalInstructions: Refill with compatible replacement ink cartridges for continuous reuse. If non-functional and cannot be repaired, dispose of the pen in the standard household trash cart (brown cart in Austin) or save with other pens and markers to drop off at an office supply store participating in the TerraCycle Writing Instruments Zero Waste program.

analyses.material: Composite synthetic textile (predominantly woven polyester / PET with nylon webbing, polyacetal/metal zippers, and polyurethane backing coating)
analyses.localAcceptanceDetails: Austin Resource Recovery (City of Austin curbside recycling) does NOT accept textiles, clothing, luggage, or backpacks in the blue curbside recycling cart. Fabric, straps, and zippers act as 'tanglers' in Materials Recovery Facilities (MRFs), wrapping around sorting screen axles and requiring manual shutdown to remove.
preparationSteps: Do not place this item in the blue curbside recycling bin.
Inspect the backpack for functionality (working zippers, intact seams, straps).
If in usable condition, clean with warm soapy water or machine wash on gentle cycle to prepare for donation.
If unusable, check for specialized textile drop-off bins or Austin's Recycle & Reuse Drop-off Center textile recovery partners.
limitations: Multi-material construction: blending of woven polyester fabric, polyurethane water-resistant coatings, metal/nylon zipper teeth, and foam padding makes mechanical separation economically and technically infeasible at MRFs.
Causes severe mechanical downtime in automated single-stream sorting facilities as strap tanglers snag spinning shafts and disc screens.
Dyes, surface treatments, and mixed synthetic fibers contaminate single-stream plastics processing streams.
analyses.safeDisposalInstructions: If still functional, donate to a local Austin charity (such as Austin Pets Alive! Thrift, Goodwill Central Texas, or local school drives). If completely worn out or damaged beyond repair, place it in the curbside brown/black trash cart for landfill disposal, or drop off at an Austin Recycle & Reuse Drop-off Center partner accepting mixed textiles.
